claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock has inherently high cooling-rate susceptibility.
AlCrFeNiSi powder processing is susceptible to thermal-gradient-induced residual stresses.
Low-energy pre-sintering followed by moderated-energy consolidation will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to entirely high-thermal-load processing.
The two-step process will improve mechanical properties relative to entirely high-thermal-load processing.
Sub-melting-temperature pre-sintering will initiate controlled neck formation between AlCrFeNiSi particles.
A pre-sintering window of approximately 400–600 °C is applicable to the proposed process.
Pre-sintered inter-particle necks will improve stress distribution during final consolidation.
Pre-sintered inter-particle necks will reduce thermal gradients during final consolidation.
Low-level diffusion bonding during pre-sintering reduces sharp thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients alleviate residual-stress buildup.
Pre-sintering will produce a more homogeneous microstructure.
Lower thermal input will minimize grain coarsening and microstructural degradation.
A pre-sintered powder bed will require less energy during final laser consolidation.
Reduced final-consolidation energy will further decrease residual-stress accumulation.
The two-step process will enhance yield strength and ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The two-step process will simplify post-processing relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The intervention is effective only for miniature components with feature sizes below 10 mm, where heat accumulation is highly localized.
Incomplete sintering or interfacial porosity may degrade the final properties of two-step-processed components.
